 La.App. No. 346 Of 2014

 Judgment

1. An extent of 0.80 Ares of land in Block No.9 of Re-Survey No.29/19 of Nedumbassery Village was acquired for the purpose of the construction of a new railway line from Angamaly to Azhutha as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 14.11.2006.

As per the revenue records, the A claimant was the Thandaper holder of the said land, but the land was taken possession from the B & C claimants, who are husband and wife, as they were in possession of the land.
Hence, the award amount of Rs.2,38,465/- was deposited in the Court under Section 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

George vs State Of Kerala on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5910482/
3 2.
A claimant alone filed claim statement.
The A claimant was examined as AW1 and Exts.A1 to A4 were marked from the side of A claimant.
From the side of B and C claimants, the C claimant was examined as CW1 and Ext.A5 document was marked.
3. After appreciation of evidence, the Reference Court passed the impugned judgment finding that the A claimant is entitled to get the award amount.
Challenging the said judgment, the B & C claimants LA.APP. NO. 346 OF 2014 2025:KER:72156 have filed the present appeal.
4. During the pendency of the appeal, the 3rd respondent/A claimant died and her legal heirs were impleaded as additional respondents 6 to 10.
Thereafter, the 7th defendant died and his legal heirs were impleaded as additional respondents 11 to 13.

The 8 th defendant died and his legal heirs were impleaded as additional respondents 14 to 16.
5.

I heard the learned counsel for the appellants, Smt. Sneha J. and Sri. K.S. Babu, the learned counsel for respondents 6, 9 & 10.
6.

The learned counsel for the appellants contended that Ext.A5 sale deed would reveal that the B &
C claimants is having 4 cents of land equivalent to 1.62 ares of land.
Even though the Re-Survey number is shown as 29/2 and 29/1/3, the old survey number stated therein is 557/1B-1.
The acquired property was in Resurvey No.29/19.
It is on record that the old Survey Number of Re-survey No.29/19 is Survey No.557/1B-1.
The acquired land was taken possession from the B & C claimants.

Hence, the acquired land could belong only to B & C claimants alone as per Ext.A5.
LA.APP. NO. 346 OF 2014 2025:KER:72156 7.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the contesting respondents contended that the acquired property is situated in Re-Survey No.29/19.
The said property was duly mutated in the name of the A claimant in her Thandaper and she has been paying land tax.

Though as per Ext.A1 title deed, the A claimant derived 45 square meters of land in old Sy. No.557/1B-1, the said land is found to be having 80 Square Meters in Re-survey and that is why the extent of 80 Square Meters was included in the Thandaper of the A claimant.
It would reveal that the A claimant is the titleholder of the acquired property.
The Reference Court correctly found in favour of the A claimant and no interference is required.
8. I have considered the rival contentions.
9. The Reference Court has found title in favour of the A claimant on the basis of Exts.A1 to A4 documents.
Ext.A1 is the sale deed of the year 1978, in which 45 square meters of land in old Survey No.557/1B-1 is scheduled.
The A claimant does not have a case that she was having excess land as per Ext.A1 sale deed.
When she was examined as AW1, she admitted that she derived only 45 Square LA.APP. NO. 346 OF 2014 2025:KER:72156 Meters of land as per Ext.A1.
When the Ext.A1 sale deed was executed, the re-survey was not completed.
It was only thereafter, the re-survey was completed.

George vs State Of Kerala on 26 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5910482/
4
On the other hand, in Ext.A5, which is a title deed of B & C claimants, the re-survey numbers stated therein are 29/2 and 29/1/3 and the old survey number stated therein is 557/1B-1.
So, it is clear that both parties were having property in old Survey No.557/1B-1.
Admittedly, the acquired property is situated in old survey No.557/1B-1.
It is also admitted that the Re-survey No.29/19 corresponds to the old survey No.557/1B-1.
Admittedly, the property was taken from the possession of the B & C claimants.
The A claimant does not have a case that any portion of her property is encroached by the B & C claimants.
The aforesaid facts would reveal that the A claimant was having only 45 square meters of land in old Survey No.557/1B-1 as per Ext.A1.
Merely because more extent of land is included in the Thandaper account, she cannot claim more extent of land when she is not having possession of the said extent of land.
Revenue records cannot confer title.
Hence, I find that the A claimant has proved title over 45 square meters of land LA.APP. NO. 346 OF 2014 2025:KER:72156 only out of the acquired property.

It is true that the property acquired from B & C claimants in LAC No.21/2007 is not disclosed before the court, but the probability is that the remaining 35 square meters of land belongs to the B & C claimants since the land was taken possession from the B & C claimants and they have property in old Survey No.557/1B-1 as per Ext.A5.

Accordingly, the impugned Order in favour of A claimant is liable to be set aside and modified to the effect that the A claimant is entitled to get compensation for 45 Square Meters of land and the B & C claimants together are entitled to get compensation for 35 Square Meters of land.

10. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed by setting aside the impugned judgment and the Reference answered, declaring that the A claimant is entitled to get an amount of Rs.1,34,137/- and the B & C claimants together are entitled to get Rs.1,04,328/- out of the amount of Rs.2,38,465/- deposited in the Court.
